mathematical_review: Standing assumptions are an actual transitive permutation action, nonidentity involutions, the string commutation relations, every maximal omission intransitive, and an endpoint anchor moved only by rho_0. No intersection property, parity, full symmetric image, primitivity or quotient-action faithfulness is used.

The noncommutation component H containing rho_0 is transitive: every other component fixes e and centralizes H, so the full G-orbit of e is e^H. Such another component then fixes every point. Nonidentity of each distinguished mark excludes that component. Hence every adjacent pair in the string fails to commute.

At a unique crossing j>0, the acquired orbit contraction gives exactly two omission orbits A,B. R=G_>j fixes e and commutes with L=G_<j. Since LR is transitive on A, L is transitive there and R fixes A pointwise. A is nontrivial. If B is a singleton, L fixes B, so the split is perfect. Otherwise nonperfection forces a left mark to move B. If none were shared, the connected left interval would have every mark supported on A, since rho_0 moves e; this contradiction supplies a shared left mark.

The exact strengthening of the oriented head interface to 2r>n is justified from its proof, not from its stronger published statement. I reread all five preliminary lemmas of acquired head_support.tex and its entire final proof. The last-mark lemma itself gives n>=2r whenever the last mark is shared, or (i>0) acts on the first side. All commuting-orbit, distance-two internal-pair, minimal-transitivity and path inequalities have no global rank assumption. Connectedness fixes the side of the remaining tail. Thus the support bound uses only 2r>n once its orientation is supplied; the separate orbit-budget orientation theorem at 2r>n+2 is not imported.

In particular the i>0 transitive-side case is h=i+1 and |A|+1>=2h+1. The intransitive cases d=1, d=2 moved/internal, and d>=3 each supply |A|+d>=2h+1, including the weak i=1,d=3 equality. The i=0 case has disjoint fixed path pieces of h+1 and h vertices. No parity-based equality exclusion enters.

There is at least one eligible edge of every colour because its omission is intransitive but the full action is transitive. If every colour had two, the complete acquired paired-cut bound would contradict 2r>n. For j=0, the anchor is an actual singleton omission orbit, so the split is perfect and 2j=|A|-1=0.

For a nonperfect least crossing j>0, reversal sends it to i-prime=r-1-j and the first original shared index g to h-prime=r-1-g. The old R fixes old A, which is the second side in the reversed oriented proof. The last-mark exclusion gives g>0; sharedness gives g<j. The support is exactly that of original G_<g. If j=r-1, the reversed cut is zero; the final reversed tail contains rho_0 and therefore lies on old A, fixing the endpoint naming without an implicit orientation choice.

Every prefix colour 0,...,g-1 is ambient-paired by minimality of j, not merely locally eligible. The prefix is a nontrivial intransitive group contained in G_j, so the acquired contiguous-interval theorem supplies 2g<=|X|-c<=|X|-1. The reversed head bound supplies 2(r-1-g)<=n-|X|-1. Their sum is exactly 2r-2<=n-2, contradicting 2r>n.

After perfection, the prefix before j is transitive on A and fixes B, hence has exactly one nontrivial orbit and support A. Applying the same actual ambient deficit gives 2j<=|A|-1. The source definition of a perfect split was checked in its retained TeX and agrees with the opposing factors fixing the opposite omission sides.

The complete acquired paired-cut proof, generic unique-crossing/fixed-prefix proof, actual minimal-transitivity/head proof, ambient interval proof and its full terminal-orbit adaptation were read. Old historical pending wording in those frozen components is not treated as a current source disposition or as a new premise.
